result.title: Physiology-Aware Graph Attention for Early Ventricular Reentry Prediction
result.summary: Sudden cardiac death mostly originates from post-infarct ventricular tachycardia. This reentry is sustained by propagation around scar tissue, but its risk remains difficult to predict from infarct imaging alone. While in silico induction studies can reveal these mechanisms, exploring many substrates and pacing locations remains computationally expensive. We propose a graph attention classifier for early prediction of sustained ventricular reentry from simulated cardiac electrophysiology. Each simulation is represented as a graph with early nodal voltage samples and edge attributes encoding geometry, stimulation frequency, tissue labels, amplitude, and diastolic interval. These descriptors are computed only from the first two paced activations, before sustained reentry is observed. On a balanced independent test set of 1000 simulations, the classifier achieves 94.6% accuracy, 95.4% sensitivity, 93.8% specificity, 94.6% F1-score, 0.987 ROC-AUC, and 0.985 PR-AUC. Ablation experiments show that diastolic interval is the most critical descriptor. Qualitative attention inspection suggests that different heads focus on border-zone, stimulation location, and early propagation path. These results support graph attention as a fast early-prediction approach for large-scale in silico ventricular reentry studies.

AI.brief_summary: 提出一种图注意力分类器，仅利用前两次起搏激活的节点电压与编码几何、刺激频率、组织标签等的边属性，在模拟心脏电生理数据上提前预测持续性室性折返是否发生，并报告了准确率等指标与消融、注意力定性分析。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「仅凭早期少量观测预测最终结局」的设定与注意力集中于决定性区域，可能为 LVR 中依据部分证据决定继续观察或提前停止（STOP）以及实体关系编码提供概念类比，可供核查；但材料未涉及视觉-语言推理或 latent 状态生成，联系仅为推测。
